why: HELD, NOT MEASURED. Opened so the hypothesis survives the session; no Forge run has been made and no figure here is evidence. Found by walking the Atlas synergy graph out from this deck's engine cards, where the heaviest edges were Counters + Tokens and Sac + Death Trigger. THE THESIS: counters are the fastest route to a big vampire in these colours, because +1/+1 counter DOUBLERS do not exist in BRW -- Ozolith, the Shattered Spire is green -- and PROLIFERATE is the colour-shifted substitute. Blade of the Bloodchief is the find and the pilot already owns it: one mana, equip one, and every creature death puts TWO counters on an equipped Vampire, which in a deck built on eating its own tokens is the fastest accelerant available. Dusk Legion Duelist converts that engine into cards, drawing whenever counters land on it, once a turn. Metastatic Evangel proliferates on every nontoken creature entering, and this deck casts about nine spells a game. ALL THREE COST ONE OR TWO MANA, which is deliberate: bloodline's only measured cost is stall rising from 5 games in 100 to 8, diagnosed as a CURVE problem against flat mana, and v4 failed trying to fix it with acceleration Forge would not cast. Cutting Vish Kal at seven, Bloodtracker at four and Unbounded Potential at two takes eight mana out of the curve while adding the counter engine. MILL WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: 89 BRW cards read an opponent's graveyard but this deck has only two payoffs and one enabler, self-mill buries the giants it is digging for, and going all-in on Altar of Dementia as a wincon is a different deck rather than an increment.

staged.why: Both proliferate and both cost the same white, but Norn's Choirmaster fires off the one thing this deck reliably does. Edgar is a first-strike haste commander who attacks every turn, and his own trigger already puts a +1/+1 counter on EACH Vampire when he swings -- so Choirmaster proliferates on top of a mass counter event rather than beside it. Metastatic Evangel keys on nontoken creatures entering, which this deck does about nine times a game but often too late to matter.
